$$
{x}^{2}-81=0\,\text{and}\,{9}^{5-x}=0.
$$

We now solve each of these equations separately.

- The equation ${x}^{2}-81=0$ can be factored as

$$
(x+9)(x-9)=0,
$$

which leads to the solutions $x=-9,9.$

- The equation ${9}^{5-x}=0$ has no solutions because ${9}^{5-x}$ is positive for every real number $x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}17{x}^{2}\cdot {9}^{x+5}+x\cdot {9}^{x+5}-5\cdot {9}^{x+5} & ={x}^{2}\cdot {9}^{x+5}+17x\cdot {9}^{x+5} \\ 17{x}^{2}\cdot {9}^{x+5}+x\cdot {9}^{x+5}-5\cdot {9}^{x+5}-{x}^{2}\cdot {9}^{x+5}-17x\cdot {9}^{x+5} & =0 \\ 16{x}^{2}\cdot {9}^{x+5}-16x\cdot {9}^{x+5}-5\cdot {9}^{x+5} & =0 \\ (16{x}^{2}-16x-5)\cdot {9}^{x+5} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We can now apply the zero product property, which states that $ab=0$ if and only if $a=0$ or $b=0.$ This gives us two equations,

$$
16{x}^{2}-16x-5=0\,\text{and}\,{9}^{x+5}=0.
$$

We now solve each of these equations separately.

- The equation $16{x}^{2}-16x-5=0$ can be factored as

$$
(4x+1)(4x-5)=0,
$$

which leads to the solutions $x=-\frac{1}{4},\frac{5}{4}.$

- The equation ${9}^{x+5}=0$ has no solutions because ${9}^{x+5}$ is positive for every real number $x.$
